provenance: safeexpr, review of the types tier: the same leak the %-formatting entry records, arriving through a friendly-looking conversion

provenance: Q5 research: ^(a+)+$ against a 29-character input takes 7.0 seconds, identically on every supported interpreter
note: The canonical catastrophic pattern, refused before it is compiled. Input-length caps are not the mitigation and this is why: the blowup is driven by the pattern's structure, so a 29-character subject already costs seven seconds and each further character roughly doubles it. The step budget cannot help either, because one matches() call is one node however long re spends inside it.

provenance: Q5 research flagged this as the shape a depth heuristic alone misses: (a|a)*$ is catastrophic at 2.4s and scores as depth 1
note: The research called this out as the one thing not to ship without. Nesting depth scores it safe because neither branch contains a repeat; the rule that catches it compares the branches of an alternation under a repeat and refuses two that describe the same language.

provenance: safeexpr, measured while building the gate: the research proposed counting unbounded repeats, and this pattern has none
note: No unbounded quantifier anywhere and still measurably slow, which the rule as originally proposed would have let straight through. The rule counts any repeat with a choice to make, so a{1,20} counts and a{2} does not.

provenance: safeexpr: the control for the ReDoS entries
note: Two adjacent unbounded repeats are not nested ones. Without this the entries above would pass against a gate that refused every pattern, which is not a gate anybody can use.

provenance: Q5 revisited at the 3.11 floor: atomic groups and possessive quantifiers exist on every supported version now
note: The same nesting as the first entry and instant rather than catastrophic, because an atomic group cannot give back what it matched.
